claims.text: Dockerfile lines 5-17: FROM sdk:10.0 AS build; WORKDIR /src; COPY global.json, Directory.Packages.props and three .csproj; RUN dotnet restore DonHang.Api/DonHang.Api.csproj; COPY three source folders; RUN dotnet publish -c Release -o /app --no-restore.
The .NET SDK image contains the compiler and build tools; running an ASP.NET Core app needs only the runtime (aspnet image), which is much smaller than the SDK image.

dotnet restore downloads the packages the projects list (versions from Directory.Packages.props); dotnet publish compiles and gathers the app and its packages into the output folder, run where the .NET runtime is installed; -c Release, -o /app, --no-restore as described.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs: dotnet restore, dotnet publish, Central Package Management

claims.text: global.json says which SDK versions the repository accepts (10.0.300 with rollForward latestFeature, i.e. a minimum plus roll-forward).

docker compose build api with no change: steps 2/11-11/11 CACHED (labels like [api build  7/11]); step 1 FROM is shown but not marked CACHED; after a blank line in Program.cs, steps up to 9/11 CACHED and 10/11, 11/11 run.

claims.text: Docker reuses a step while it and every step before it are unchanged; once one step changes, every later step runs again. Changing DonHang.Api.csproj invalidates 6/11 and all later steps; 1-5 are reused.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: build cache invalidation (COPY checksums)

claims.text: With the same SDK version and sources, dotnet publish in the image builds the same app from the same commands as on a developer machine, and the output runs outside a container too.
The SDK used comes from the image, not from the machine, so builds using the same image use the same SDK (the sdk:10.0 tag itself moves with each .NET patch).
claims.source_hint: .NET docs: container image tags updated on patch releases

claims.text: Pulling an image downloads only layers the machine does not already have; a new machine downloads the whole image.
-c Release selects the Release build configuration (optimised, not for debugging); the Dockerfile has a second stage named final whose steps also appear in docker compose build api output.
